newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African pension trustees need training - Marcus.
newsitem.headline: S.African pension trustees need training - Marcus.

text.p: Trustees managing assets worth over 500 billion rand ($111.7 billion) for pension funds on behalf of some 10 million South Africans should receive training immediately, deputy finance minister Gill Marcus said on Monday.

Addressing the Institute of Retirement Funds' annual conference Marcus said there was no legislation regarding trusteeship and few guidelines for qualifications to be appointed a trustee of a pension fund.
The National Retirement Consultative Forum had recommended that an independent Institute of Training for Boards of Management/Trustees should be set up, she said.

"This need not wait for a white paper process, but could, and perhaps should, be an initiative of the life and pensions industry. This could be established immediately. You have the resources and there is no question about the need," she said.
The process forward from the consultative forum was still being discussed in the finance department, Marcus said, adding the department's approach would be made known "in the very near future".

She also urged the retirement fund industry to make its views known as soon as possible on the King Report on insider trading -- released earlier this month -- so that findings could be submitted to the finance minister.
"...this report also again raises the fragmented nature of the supervisory and regulatory environment," Marcus said.
She said the government, guided by the Financial Services Board, had short term projects to protect investors and ensure a secure environment.

These included a revamping of legislation for collective investment schemes, strengthening legislation to combat insider trading and legislation to regulate the wholesale market and dealers in exchange-listed and unlisted securities.
